We are the leading investor in prevention in South Carolina. Our innovative evidence-backed prevention model is working every day for children, families and communities.

© Copyright 2025 | Children’s Trust of South Carolina is the statewide organization focused on the prevention of child abuse and neglect. We provide funding, resources and training to help local program partners build strong families and positive childhoods.

As an intermediary organization focused on prevention, Children’s Trust is the statewide advocate for issues critical to South Carolina’s children. We provide resources and technical support to our prevention partners and create and share messages about prevention. We award grants to private nonprofit organizations and qualified state agencies to fund a broad range of innovative child abuse and neglect prevention programs to meet the critical needs of South Carolina’s children. We also support and fund proven prevention programs, conduct high-quality data and trend analysis, and offer training

In the unique position of a state-sanctioned non-profit with a governor-appointed board of directors , we leverage federal, state and private funding to maximize prevention investments in South Carolina. We are the South Carolina home to the South Carolina Home Visiting Coalition, Adverse Childhood Experiences Initiative, KIDS COUNT, the National Family Support Network, and Triple P South Carolina.
As an intermediary organization, we work alongside our partners and stakeholders in communities across the state to deliver proven prevention programs.

Children’s Trust helps determine which models to use and where the need is the greatest. We work hand-in hand with our partners guiding them through the technical aspects of delivering evidence-based programs, providing coaching and technical assistance.

Defenders For Children is dedicated to protecting and saving children from abuse, exploitation, trafficking, online victimization, and other crimes against our most vulnerable.

Through education, advocacy, community engagement, and legislative efforts, we work to prevent child victimization, strengthen child protection laws, support law enforcement, and stop predators before they can harm another child. Our mission is to empower families, educate children and adults, and inspire communities to take an active role in creating a safer future for every child. ​

We accomplish our mission by creating innovative programs and public awareness initiatives that educate communities about child abuse prevention, online safety, human trafficking, responsible parenting, and protecting children from sextortion and exploitation. Through our websites, social media platforms, public service announcements, educational campaigns, community events, training programs, and strategic partnerships, we provide resources that encourage adults, teens, businesses, schools, civic organizations, and communities to become active participants in protecting children.

Together with law enforcement, community leaders, corporate partners, volunteers, and supporters, Defenders For Children is building a nationwide movement that protects children, strengthens communities, supports those on the front lines, and ensures every child has the opportunity to grow up safe, secure, and free from abuse.

At the heart of our mission is our nationally recognized Electronic Storage Detection (ESD) K9 Program, through which we fundraise for, train, and donate highly specialized K9 teams to law enforcement agencies across the United States.

These extraordinary K9s use their remarkable sense of smell to locate hidden electronic storage devices containing critical digital evidence in child exploitation investigations while also serving as certified therapy dogs, providing comfort and emotional support to child victims, investigators, and first responders. By equipping agencies with these life-saving resources, we help uncover vital evidence, rescue victims, strengthen investigations, and bring offenders to justice.

Landmarks for Families provides temporary and longer-term residential care through two cottages on our North Charleston campus: Ledford House and NuHouse. Ledford House serves high-school-aged youth in foster care, while NuHouse provides transitional residential care for older youth preparing for adulthood.

Our trauma-informed residential programs use the evidence-based Teaching Family Model to provide comprehensive, individualized support for each youth’s educational, emotional, physical, and social needs. We work closely with youth, families, the South Carolina Department of Social Services, and other members of each youth’s support team to connect youth with supportive relationships, skills, resources, and opportunities. New Morning is here to make sure birth control access is simple, safe, and affordable for every woman in South Carolina. We are a leader in the state and the only organization exclusively dedicated to fulfilling this critical mission.
We provide free and low-cost birth control to women who are low-income and uninsured through telehealth and our vast network of partner sites across the state.
We offer in-person and virtual training opportunities, accredited and free, for clinicians and healthcare staff across South Carolina and beyond.

We are for women’s futures. Bright horizons and limitless opportunities. The ability to build a full life of school and work, family and friends, travel and passions. We are for women who go their own way, thriving inside the worlds they imagine and create.

Barriers in our state like high concentrations of poverty and challenging provider access in rural areas make our work especially critical. We are the largest and longest-running state initiative doing this work in the U.S.

Our work is made possible by a network of passionate people, from our dedicated team to our vast network of nonprofit clinical partners. We stand united in our mission to ensure that every woman in South Carolina can access the reproductive healthcare she needs.

Educating the general public is a critical component of our program. We provide medically accurate information about family planning and affordable contraception through our statewide consumer education campaign, No Drama.

Better tools for providers lead to better reproductive healthcare outcomes for women. We are investing in a healthcare workforce equipped to serve women in all corners of the state—an investment that is especially crucial amid skyrocketing demand for contraceptive services and a growing provider shortage.
Understand our real-world impact and discover how we are transforming reproductive healthcare and empowering women and families in South Carolina.

New Morning is a South Carolina nonprofit that works to increase individuals’ equitable access to family planning in order to empower women and couples to plan whether or when to start or expand their families and shape their own futures. We train and support a statewide alliance of nonprofit healthcare partners who provide free and low-cost contraceptive services including education, counseling and a wide range of birth control methods.

No. New Morning does not fund abortion services or pharmaceutical products that cause abortions. We work to increase birth control access by connecting patients to contraceptive care at local partner clinics — which research has shown actually decreases unintended pregnancies and abortions.

New Morning is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, and our ability to help South Carolina women and couples avoid unwanted pregnancies and plan families on their terms primarily depends upon the generosity of individuals and foundations. Charitable donations to New Morning are tax-deductible.
Explore ways that you can help support our mission .

For low-income and uninsured women, New Morning provides access to a wide range of FDA-approved birth control methods, including non-hormonal IUD, hormonal IUD, implant, pills, vaginal ring, patch, and the birth control “shot”. Visit NoDrama.org to compare contraceptive methods and find the best option for you.

The South Carolina Coalition Against Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault (SCCADVASA) serves as the collective voice promoting the prevention of domestic violence and sexual assault in South Carolina.

CEUs offered by our training courses vary depending on the topic and audience. Consult the training announcement/flyer for information about which CEUs are offered for the training in question. SCCADVASA collaborates with the professional licensing and accrediting agencies that govern the credits awarded for attendance. We provide the training and track your attendance, but do not have the authority to grant or deny the credits to your record.

We are an independent 501(c)(3) non-profit organization , but our approach is highly collaborative with our 22 domestic and sexual violence members who provide direct services in communities across the state, affiliates, partners, and allies. SCCADVASA is an active member of several national domestic and sexual violence networks, and we work in partnership with Coalitions in all 50 states and several US territories.

We’ve developed this infographic (click to download a PDF) to provide an overview of how our work, and the work of our member organizations, impacts survivors of domestic and sexual violence. It is our hope that this will provide a greater understanding of how we work together towards a South Carolina free from domestic and sexual violence.

We provide our member organizations, affiliates and allied organizations with the support and technical assistance they need to help them better serve survivors in their communities. For the domestic violence and sexual assault member organizations, this support includes collaboration through member meetings and interest groups, campaign resources and publication access, along with continued education though trainings and webinars on revolving topics. org_description.value: Learn about Young Moms Together, a nonprofit helping young mothers with housing, healthcare, education, and parenting skills for a better future.

From housing and healthcare to education and emotional support, we walk alongside each woman as she builds a healthy, empowered life for herself and her child. We provide complete, wraparound support through our program.

We support academic progress, GED completion, vocational training, and job readiness— equipping young women with the skills and confidence needed to complete their education and achieve financial stability.
We provide stable housing through our licensed group home and rental assistance program— ensuring young mothers and their children have a safe place to live while building toward independence.

Many of the young women we serve are aging out of foster care , fleeing unsafe homes, or sleeping in cars with their babies— despite working or attending school. They’re turned away from leases because they have no rental history. Denied housing because they can’t find a co-signer. And they face discrimination simply for being young, single moms.
